task_instance: Created a small sample TypeScript repository (sample_repo/) with a fake .git/config and .git/HEAD plus src/inventory.ts, src/orderService.ts, src/index.ts implementing an Inventory/OrderService model. Asked the wiki-qa question 'How does order fulfillment reduce inventory stock, and what happens if stock is insufficient?' and answered it by reading the source files and synthesizing a grounded Markdown answer (answer.md) with linked citations, a Key Files table, and a Mermaid sequence diagram, following the skill's Response Format and Rules.
evidence: Files produced under the work directory: sample_repo/.git/config, sample_repo/.git/HEAD, sample_repo/src/inventory.ts, sample_repo/src/orderService.ts, sample_repo/src/index.ts, and answer.md. Source-repo resolution step (which the skill normally does via `git remote get-url origin` and `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`) was performed instead by reading .git/config and .git/HEAD as plain text files, since shell/git commands are not available in this runtime but text-file reading is -- this substitution kept the skill's core requirement (resolve REPO_URL and branch, choose linked-citation format) intact without using a shell. Found remote 'https://github.com/example-org/sample-inventory.git' and branch 'main' from those files. Then read the three source files directly (Read tool) and wrote answer.md, which: cites exact file:line locations as clickable links in the resolved REPO_URL/blob/BRANCH/file#Lline format, includes a 'Key Files' table with linked File column, includes a Mermaid sequence diagram of the fulfillment/error-propagation flow, uses a fenced TypeScript code block quoting the actual removeStock method, and bases every claim strictly on the created source files (no external knowledge). Verified by re-reading answer.md back and cross-checking each citation and code excerpt against the actual line numbers/content in inventory.ts and orderService.ts -- all matched. No shell/Bash tool, no code execution, no binary files, and no MCP/connector tools were used at any point; only Read and Write on text files inside the work directory.
